_doc: Exceptions to the trader-facing claim provenance guard.
Read src/test/claimProvenance.test.ts for the contract. In short: a literal
that matches a claim marker must appear here with a category and a real
answer to 'where did this come from'.
DERIVED - computed from this trader's own data; source names the producer
CITED   - external claim with a primary source; source is the citation
FIXTURE - demo data mirroring a real API field; source names the field
There is no UNSOURCED category. If a claim has no provenance the fix is to
DELETE it, not to describe it here. This file starting nearly empty is the
point: the 2026-09-03 audit found 26 claims and zero sources, and every one
of them was removed rather than written down.
literal_sha256 is the first 16 hex chars of sha256 over the extracted
literal. The test prints the hash of anything it rejects.
_empty: It is empty, and that is the correct state.
The first draft carried one LEGAL entry for the SEBI references in
PrivacyPolicy.tsx. Narrowing the SEBI markers to require an attribution
verb or a data noun removed the need for it: naming the regulator is not a
claim about what the regulator has measured. Eight legal-disclaimer hits
went with it. A marker that forces honest text into an allowlist is a
broken marker, and fixing the marker beats writing the exception down.
Everything the guard found on the way in was DELETED, not allowlisted.
